config.style: half-timbered Tudor cottage: white plaster + dark timber frame with diagonal braces, 45-deg red slate roof with wedge gables, brick chimney, 4x7 segmented-wall doorway, cross-muntin windows on 3 faces

steps: get_references half-timbered cottage (2 photos studied: steep tiled roof, dark timber grid on white plaster, brick chimney)
Built shell at x=150: floor slab, front/back/side walls segmented around door (4x7) and three 6x4 window openings
Roof: two 45-deg slabs meeting at ridge y=19 + 4 WedgePart gable triangles + ridge beam
Details: timber frame (horizontals, studs, corner posts, diagonal braces), door+frame+lintel+knob+step, glass+frame+muntin windows, brick chimney with cap
capture_angles round 1: timbers/window frames buried inside wall thickness - pushed all trim proud of wall faces
capture_angles round 2: all angles read as coherent cottage; stopped

recipe.text: Recipe: segment walls into parts around openings (never overlay), wedge gables oriented apex-inward at z=+/-4 with yaw 180 on one side, roof slabs at 45deg with slopeLen 12.8 covering half-span+overhang. Trim must sit PROUD of the wall plane (z 8.15 vs wall face 8.0) or it vanishes into the plaster - first capture caught this. Half-timber look = Concrete plaster + Wood beams 0.5-0.6 thick + 2 diagonal braces; Slate roof material at Color 146,74,54 reads as terracotta tile. 71 parts, no meshes, no save_mesh needed.
